draft.title: The external environment
card: The external environment is made up of forces outside a business that it cannot control. Because it cannot change them, a business must respond to them.
wider forces that affect all businesses and that no single business can influence, such as the economy, laws, government policy, technology and changes in society.
the customers, suppliers and competitors a business deals with directly, so it differs from one business to the next.
Responding means adapting, such as changing prices, products or plans. An owner cannot stop a new law or a rival opening nearby, but can plan for it.
draft.remember: Macro forces touch every business. The operating environment is its own customers, suppliers and competitors.

a.q: A new Victorian café is planning ahead. Which of these is an external factor it must respond to?
opts: A new law on how food must be labelled
The skills of the café's own staff
The owner's choice of opening hours
The range of meals the café decides to sell
a.why: A new law comes from outside the café and the owner cannot change it, only respond. Staff skills, opening hours and the menu are choices the business makes itself, so they are not external.
a.clue: Which one could the owner not change by making a decision?

b.q: Priya's bike shop in Ballarat faces a new rival bike store that opens across the street. Where does this sit?
opts: Operating environment, outside Priya's control
Macro environment, outside Priya's control
Operating environment, within Priya's control
Internal environment, within Priya's control
b.why: A competitor is part of the operating environment, the customers, suppliers and competitors a business deals with directly. Priya cannot stop it opening, so it is outside her control. It is not the macro environment, because one new store does not affect all businesses.
b.clue: Does this rival affect every business, or mainly shops like Priya's?

a.best: A new law on how food must be labelled

proposal.title: The external environment
card: The external environment is made up of factors outside a business that it cannot control. Factors it does control, such as its staff, products and opening hours, are internal.
the wider forces that act on many businesses at once, well beyond any one firm's own market.
the customers, suppliers and competitors a business deals with directly, so it differs from one business to the next.
A business cannot stop external changes, but it must plan for them and respond, such as by changing prices, products or plans. An owner cannot block a new law or a rival opening nearby.
proposal.remember: A business cannot control external factors, so it plans and adapts. Macro forces are wide, operating factors are close to the business.
